query: Consider the following context: Temper embrittlement, characterized by a dramatic loss of ductility within a narrow temperature window, is ubiquitous in conventional alloys but is not reported in compositionally complex or high‐entropy alloy systems. In that context, which material can be used for ductile–brittle–ductile transition, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A compositionally complex alloy system, specifically a high-entropy alloy, will exhibit a ductile–brittle–ductile transition when subjected to a systematic temperature variation experiment combined with molecular dynamics simulations, due to its inherent resistance to temper embrittlement.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloy in its initial, untested state
generation.intervention: Systematic temperature variation experiment combined with molecular dynamics simulations
generation.conditions: Varied temperatures, specifically within the narrow temperature window where temper embrittlement occurs in conventional alloys
generation.structural_mediator: The complex, multi-component crystal structure of the high-entropy alloy
generation.mechanism: The ability of the high-entropy alloy to resist temper embrittlement and maintain its ductility across a wide temperature range, including the narrow temperature window where conventional alloys exhibit a dramatic loss of ductility
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% increase in ductility relative to conventional alloys within the narrow temperature window, with a standard deviation of 5%
generation.boundary: The narrow temperature window where temper embrittlement occurs in conventional alloys
generation.uncertainty: The exact composition and processing conditions of the high-entropy alloy may affect its resistance to temper embrittlement and ductile–brittle–ductile transition

falsification_experiment.design: A systematic temperature variation experiment combined with molecular dynamics simulations on a high-entropy alloy and a conventional alloy, with measurements of ductility and microstructure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the high-entropy alloy exhibits a ductility decrease of more than 20% within the narrow temperature window, the hypothesis is falsified
